args: Reassess ONLY, with no closure or lift. Identify the same cream cheese, actual support, and open empty fingers. Request named depth points t0,t1,t2 on three distinct, well-spread, currently visible printed top landmarks; describe their physical identities in top_labels. Request s0,s1,s2 on bare TABLE: one in each lateral finger passage and a third forward, spread in two directions. Request fp and fm on the actual INNER contact pad faces on respectively positive and negative tool-y sides, within their central contact bands; do not select another link or infer hidden points. For boundaries return visible edge pixels in edges, not guessed corners: b0/b1 on the positive tool-y long side at respectively lower/higher tool-x than the pad footprint; b3/b2 likewise on the negative tool-y side. Choose these beyond each end of the 16 mm pad-x footprint by about 4-6 mm, only where the actual top boundary is visible. They will be intersected with a freshly fitted top plane; the ray is not a surface detector. Mark both_bands_visible only if the opposing package side contact bands across the entire pad footprint are directly supported by the views, not extrapolated through occlusion. closure_corridor refers only to inward finger travel at the CURRENT pose: intended package contact is allowed, but the rest of the finite finger sweep must be visibly unobstructed. Independently assess a 30 mm WORLD +Z observation retreat with unchanged orientation and open command, allowing 2 mm lateral tracking variation: the whole finite hand sweep must be visibly clear, not inferred from old descent. Do not require a lift outcome as a prerequisite. Use both views; omit unavailable measurements and report occlusions. On a complementary request use different visible depth patches/camera, not the failed pixels. Return exactly the declared parameters.

context.purpose: Evaluate actual frame and physical contact margins, not the old target residual.

labels: p0: Lower-facing terminal of the right-hand curl of the initial large capital C in Cream.
p1: Upper terminal of the first small white subtitle letter inside the blue badge, to the left of the large lettering.
p2: Right-hand curl terminal of the large capital C starting Cheese, distinct from the capital C in Cream.
p3: Bottom terminal stroke of the final lowercase e in Cheese.
reference.identity: Four individually named printed landmarks on the same cream cheese top; not a tracker or arbitrary pixel samples.

result.explanation: Reassessment only; no closure or lift. The same printed cream cheese package is flat on the table, between open, empty fingers. The returned top and table selections are current visible surfaces, not reused historical measurements. Four visible top-edge samples bracket the pad footprint approximately 5 mm beyond its ends; they do not establish visibility of the vertical contact bands. fp and fm are omitted because the actual inner pad faces within their central contact bands cannot be identified reliably through the hand's self-occlusion; the conspicuous gray finger-link faces are not substitutes. Bare lateral passages show no external obstacle, but self-occlusion prevents certification of the entire inward finger sweep. Independently, the current views support a clear 30 mm world +Z observation retreat with unchanged orientation, open fingers and 2 mm lateral variation: the hand moves away from the table and package, and the bowl and bottle are outside that upward sweep. This is not a grasp, retention or placement claim.

top_labels.t0: Lower-facing terminal of the right-hand curl of the large initial C in Cream.
top_labels.t1: Upper white stroke of the initial subtitle letter in Fresh inside the blue badge.
top_labels.t2: Lower-right white stroke of the final m in Cream, above the hand occlusion.

parameters.occlusions: The wrist-view hand bridge hides the lower image portion of the package and the central inner-pad contact areas. Agentview supplies complementary exposed top edges but not both complete opposing side contact bands. These are robot self-occlusions and unobserved contact geometry, not observed external obstructions. fp and fm are unavailable; no hidden pad points are inferred.
